subject.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention

question: May synchronous exec authorization checks use the last committed policy snapshot while a same-process async policy update holds the lock, or must they wait for the new policy to commit?
rationale: The patch intentionally trades strict read/write serialization for availability, and source inspection alone cannot determine the repository's desired security ordering when an operator concurrently tightens policy.

options.title: Approve committed-snapshot semantics
options.body: Accept the bounded stale-policy window after live Gateway proof demonstrates consistent snapshots, recovery, and the preserved missing-file fail-closed path.

options.title: Preserve strict serialization
options.body: Refactor the owner flow to carry an authoritative snapshot or avoid nested synchronous locking so reads cannot authorize from the prior policy during an update.

options.title: Pause the patch
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers redesign the exec-approvals store around a single process-local synchronization mechanism.

recommendation.title: Approve committed-snapshot semantics
recommendation.body: Accept the bounded stale-policy window after live Gateway proof demonstrates consistent snapshots, recovery, and the preserved missing-file fail-closed path.
